Select unrelated individuals by criteria

Source: R/rkn_select_criteria.R
rkn_select_criteria.Rd

Selects a maximum set of unrelated individuals, as rkn_select_random does, but makes the choices that the network leaves open by criteria on the covariates instead of at random. Each family is resolved on its own: families of up to 5 members through the structural rules in rules_db, larger families through structural reductions followed by a search of what remains; the returned object is as for rkn_select_random(). How the criteria are evaluated in large families, exactly or on a sample of maximum sets, is described in the section Search over maximum sets of rkn_selection. With optimal = TRUE, the structural rules are skipped and the criteria choose among all the maximum sets of each family.

Covariates referenced by the criteria are read from the vertex attributes of g. The criteria express preferences for individuals, such as women or people younger than 50; for a target composition of the whole selection, such as half women or a mean age, see rkn_select_global.

Usage

rkn_select_criteria(
  g,
  criterion_primary,
  criterion_secondary = NULL,
  optimal = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  diagnostics = TRUE
)

Arguments

g

An igraph object. Vertex names must be stored in V(g)$name. Vertex attributes cannot be named degree, max_path_length or .name: these names are reserved for the structural measures computed during the selection. The network is usually built with rkn_graph_from_kinship, which also checks the samples; for a network built in another way, see rkn_check_samples.

criterion_primary

A criterion, created by rkn_criterion_level or rkn_criterion_cutoff, used to score candidate resolutions within each family.

criterion_secondary

Optional rkn_criterion object used to break ties in criterion_primary.

optimal

Logical. If FALSE (default), structural rules decide part of each family before the criteria are applied, and some of them fix individuals regardless of the criteria (for instance, they keep the individual at the end of a chain of relatives); the result is the best maximum set among those compatible with the rules. If TRUE, the criteria are evaluated over all the maximum sets of each family, exactly, or as described in the section Search over maximum sets of rkn_selection when the covariate has missing values. Families too intricate for this computation are selected as with optimal = FALSE and reported in the column optimal of family_summary.

seed

Optional integer, as in rkn_select_random: a seed is drawn from it for each family. Random numbers are used only to break exact ties in the criterion scores.

diagnostics

Logical. If TRUE (default), the returned object also records how each individual and each family was resolved (node_diagnostics and family_summary), which print(), summary() and plot(type = "diagnostics") use. Diagnostics increase the run time and the size of the returned object: computing the inclusion probabilities makes a selection two to three times slower in family studies, though hardly slower in population cohorts. On very large networks, or when many selections are drawn, diagnostics = FALSE returns the selection alone.

Value

An object of class rkn_selection, as for rkn_select_random; its criteria element holds the criteria.

Computation time

On one core of a laptop (Apple M2), the selection took about as long as rkn_select_random(uniform = FALSE): 1.6 seconds for a population cohort of 10,000 samples, 17 seconds for 100,000 and 32 seconds for a family study of 10,000; with optimal = TRUE, 5.5 seconds, 1 minute and 67 seconds.

See also

rkn_selection, summary.rkn_selection, plot.rkn_selection, rkn_select_random, rkn_select_global, rkn_criterion_level, rkn_criterion_cutoff, rules_db.

Examples

# A small relatedness network: two parents and their child (P1, P2, C1), a pair of
# siblings (S1, S2), three mutually related individuals (T1, T2, T3), a larger family
# (parents D1 and D2, their children K1 and K2, and K3, born to D2 and D3, a
# half-sibling of K1 and K2) and an unrelated individual (U1).
g <- igraph::graph_from_literal(P1 - C1 - P2, S1 - S2, T1 - T2 - T3 - T1,
                                D1 - K1 - D2, D1 - K2 - D2, K1 - K2,
                                D2 - K3 - D3, K1 - K3, K2 - K3, U1)
sex <- c(P1 = "F", C1 = "M", P2 = "M", S1 = "M", S2 = "F", T1 = "M", T2 = "F", T3 = "M",
         D1 = "M", K1 = "F", D2 = "F", K2 = "M", K3 = "F", D3 = "M", U1 = "F")
age <- c(P1 = 52, C1 = 21, P2 = 55, S1 = 34, S2 = 31, T1 = 60, T2 = 33, T3 = 29,
         D1 = 63, K1 = 35, D2 = 61, K2 = 38, K3 = 30, D3 = 58, U1 = 44)
igraph::V(g)$sex <- unname(sex[igraph::V(g)$name])
igraph::V(g)$age <- unname(age[igraph::V(g)$name])
# Where the structure of a family leaves a choice, prefer women ...
rkn_select_criteria(g, rkn_criterion_level("sex", "F"), seed = 1)$kept
#> [1] "P1" "P2" "S2" "T2" "D3" "D1" "D2" "U1"

# ... evaluating the criterion over all the maximum sets of each family ...
rkn_select_criteria(g, rkn_criterion_level("sex", "F"), seed = 1, optimal = TRUE)$kept
#> [1] "P1" "P2" "S2" "T2" "D1" "D2" "D3" "U1"

# ... or prefer individuals younger than 40
rkn_select_criteria(g, rkn_criterion_cutoff("age", 40, prefer = "below"), seed = 1)$kept
#> [1] "P1" "P2" "S2" "T2" "D3" "D1" "D2" "U1"

# A secondary criterion breaks the ties left by the primary one
sel <- rkn_select_criteria(g, rkn_criterion_level("sex", "F"),
                           rkn_criterion_cutoff("age", 40, prefer = "below"), seed = 1)
sel
#> <rkn_selection> Criteria-based selection (level, then cutoff), seed 1
#> Call: rkn_select_criteria(g = g, criterion_primary = rkn_criterion_level("sex", "F"), criterion_secondary = rkn_criterion_cutoff("age", 40, prefer = "below"), seed = 1)
#> Individuals: 15 | selected: 8 (53.3%)
#> Families: 5 | size min/mean/max: 1 / 3.00 / 6
#> Families with up to 5 members: 4 | with 6 or more: 1
#> Families resolved by a search over maximum sets: 1
